summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Koshin Suzuki completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also held a research post attested between 1995 and 1998.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, Koshiro Tamaki studied at Fifth Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Toyo University (1954), the University of Tokyo (professor, 1964–1976), Tohoku University (~1976–1979), and Nihon University (1979–1986).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Kosho Kawamura studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi, Nichijin Sakamoto, Shunkyo Katsumata, Koshiro Tamaki, and Yoshiro Tamura. He held several posts at Toyo University and taught at Minobusan University and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Kosho Mizutani studied at Ryukoku University (~1951–1956) and Bukkyo University. He served Bukkyo University as an assistant professor (~1956) and president (~1977–1989), and headed the boards of Tokai Gakuen and Bukkyo Kyoiku Gakuen.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Kosho Uchiyama earned a master's in Western philosophy at Waseda University and studied under Kodo Sawaki in 1941. He taught at Miyazaki Catholic Seminary (~1937–1939) and served as abbot of Antai-ji (1965–1975).
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Koshu Itabashi studied at Sendai Daiichi High School, the Imperial Japanese Naval Academy (~1943–1945), and Tohoku University (~1948–1953) under Teruji Ishizu.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Kosuke Nakazawa was affiliated with the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra in 2001 and served as professor (attested 2001) and professor emeritus (attested 2026) at Rissho University.

An Indology scholar, Kota Parameswara Aithal studied at Maharaja's Sanskrit College, Mysore, A.P. College of Arts and Commerce, and Karnatak University. He served as curator at Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1965–1972) and professor of Indology at Heidelberg University (attested 1974).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Kotatsu Fujita studied at the University of Tokyo and Harvard. He held professorships at Hokkaido University (~1967–1992) and served as president of Sapporo Otani Junior College (1992).
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Kotetsu Yoshida held posts attested in 2014 as professor emeritus at Taisho University and advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute.
A scholar of Buddhist studies, Koun Kajiyoshi completed studies at the University of Tokyo and held a post at Taisho University.

Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Koun Yamada studied at the First Higher School and trained under several teachers, including Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani in 1950. He founded Kamakura Haku-un-kai in 1953 and succeeded Yasutani from 1961 to 1989.
Working in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, Koyo Sakaino founded Bukkyo Seito Doshikai and held posts at Toyo University (~1918–1933) and Komazawa University.
A Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi, Koyo Shimizu served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University, attested in 1995.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Japanology, Koyu Tamura studied at the University of Tokyo (1949–1989). He served at the Department of Cultural Affairs (1962), Nishogakusha University (1965), and held posts at Toyo University from 1972, becoming professor emeritus (1977–2000).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Kozen Shaku studied under Senmyō. He served as abbot of Gyokuri-ji (1870–1881) and Sange-ji (1882), taught at Nagano Prefectural Northern Chugakurin (1881), and founded Shakuson Shofukai in 1893.

Working in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, Kozui Otani studied at Kyoritsu Gakusha, Gakushuin, and under Keiun Maeda. He became a fellow of the Royal Geographical Society (~1902) and served as 22nd Abbot of Nishi Hongan-ji (1903–1914).
Working in the fields of Indology and history/archaeology, Kripa Shankar Shukla held academic appointments at the University of Lucknow until 1959 and was attested there again in 1976.

An Indologist, Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya was educated at Sanskrit College and University and Presidency University (~1857–1860). He held posts at Presidency University (1862–1872) and Surendranath College (1891–1903).

An Indologist, Krishna Kanta Handiqui studied at Sanskrit College and University, the University of Calcutta, Oxford, Paris, and Berlin. He served as Principal of Jorhat College (1930–1948) and Vice-Chancellor of Gauhati University (1948–1957).
